title: stream heartbeat + cancellation coordination for Go SDK streaming ergonomics
creator: Asha Patel
description: Improve the Go SDK streaming surface to make context cancellation and timeouts predictable for long-lived streams and high-latency networks. Add a keepalive/heartbeat mechanism, per-message recv timeouts, and clear guidance/examples for client code patterns to avoid goroutine leaks and cancellation races.
motivation: Customers running Redwood streams in unreliable networks or behind load balancers see long-lived connections silently drop or block goroutines when parent contexts are cancelled. Existing examples focus on coarse deadline propagation and retries but do not cover keepalive, per-message deadlines, or user ergonomics for resuming partial streams. This work reduces support load and developer confusion, and improves reliability for Private/Dedicated customers with strict latency SLOs.
background: Existing tickets have explored context timeout propagation and stream teardown patterns, but reviewers still report two classes of problems: 1) long waits for underlying net.Conn reads to unblock when a context is cancelled, and 2) unclear user code patterns leading to goroutine leaks when users spawn per-stream readers without cancellation coordination. We need an SDK-level primitive and examples that address both.
proposal: 1) Add an optional keepalive/heartbeat probe driven by the client SDK to detect stalled connections and trigger retry/resume logic. 2) Change the streaming API to expose Recv(ctx) semantics where each received token/fragment honors the passed context (user can cancel per-message). 3) Provide a Stream.CloseWithReason(err) helper to surface graceful shutdown reasons to calling code. 4) Document recommended idioms: cancellable iterator pattern, select-loop with heartbeat, backoff/retry with resume token, and handling of deadline squashing when creating derived contexts.
api_changes: Introduce type StreamReader with method Recv(ctx context.Context) (Fragment, error)
Add StreamReader.HeartbeatStart(interval time.Duration) error -- optional keepalive from SDK to server or local ping detection
Add StreamReader.CloseWithReason(err error) to allow graceful close and metric tagging
Deprecate older blocking Next() without context in favor of Recv(ctx) ergonomics
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Implement Recv(ctx) adapter around existing grpc/http stream layer that uses connection-level read deadlines and context cancellation. Phase 2: Add heartbeat ping timer that issues lightweight pings (or no-op reads) to surface broken connections. Phase 3: Add CloseWithReason and retrofit Console/observability hooks to emit close reason metrics. Phase 4: Provide user-facing examples and update README and CHANGELOG.
technical_notes:
- Use net.Conn.SetReadDeadline for raw connections when available; for gRPC use context-aware Recv with CancelFunc and deadlines to avoid indefinite Read blocks.
- Heartbeat implemented as sent 'nop' frames when server supports it; fallback to local deadline checks and reconnect if no progress.
- Avoid internal goroutine per-message; prefer single reader goroutine with channel fan-out and explicit cancellation tokens to avoid leaks.
- For resume semantics, persist last acked message id/token and expose ResumeFrom(token) on client constructor.
tradeoffs:
- Adding heartbeat increases small amount of client-side traffic and complexity; default is off to avoid needless pings for users who don't need it.
- Per-message contexts give users maximum control but require careful docs to prevent overuse (e.g., short-lived contexts per token causing thrashing).
- Changing API surface (deprecating Next()) requires migration docs and a grace period.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes Recv(ctx) and CloseWithReason APIs in public Go package
Under simulated packet loss (30% drop) a long-lived stream recovers within configured retries when heartbeat enabled
No goroutine leaks in examples (validated by unit tests + race detector) when parent context is canceled
Integration tests demonstrate per-message deadline cancellation without leaving reader blocked
Documentation has two runnable examples: cancellable iterator and heartbeat-enabled resume flow
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for Recv(ctx) covering cancellation before, during, and after network read.
- Integration tests using a flaky proxy that drops connections to validate heartbeat & resume.
- Leak detection using t.Parallel and runtime.NumGoroutine assertions in tests.
- Fuzz per-message deadline handling to catch race conditions.
- Manual verification with dedicated cluster under Load Balancer (simulate idle timeouts).
docs_and_examples: Example 1: Cancellable iterator pattern using ctx passed into Recv(ctx) and a defer cancel in consumer
Example 2: Heartbeat + resume: show how to enable heartbeat, capture last fragment token, and call ResumeFrom(token)
FAQ: Why per-message timeouts vs. parent context? Guidance on when to use each
release_notes_blurb: Improved Go streaming ergonomics: per-message context-aware Recv(), optional heartbeat for long-lived streams, graceful CloseWithReason, and new examples for cancellation-safe patterns.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind env var REDWOOD_GO_STREAM_HEARTBEAT default off. Roll out to canary users in Dedicated/private regions, monitor goroutine counts and stream close reasons, then enable by default in 2 weeks if stable.
monitoring_and_alerts: Emit metrics: stream_heartbeat_sent, stream_heartbeat_missed, stream_close_reason, stream_resume_attempts. Add alert when heartbeat_missed > 5% for a rolling 1h window.
risks: Incorrect use of SetReadDeadline may interfere with underlying transport libraries. Server must support lightweight keepalive/ping for best results; otherwise client will fall back to reconnect heuristics.
